name: Schwarz Group
desc: Retail group operating the Lidl discount supermarket and Kaufland hypermarket chains, plus recycling and IT services businesses.
markets: Lidl stores in about 30 European countries and the United States; Kaufland in Germany and Central and Eastern Europe.
rationale: Huge European consumer reach and an existing habit of big football sponsorships; F1 could support Lidl brand building in Europe and the US.

name: Cargill, Incorporated
desc: Trades, processes and distributes grain, oilseeds, meat and other agricultural commodities, and supplies food ingredients and animal nutrition.
markets: Operates across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Africa; customers are food makers, farmers, feed producers and retailers.
rationale: Mostly B2B commodity business with little consumer branding; F1 could serve client hospitality, but the fit is weak.

name: Koch Industries, Inc.
desc: Diversified industrial group spanning refining, chemicals, pulp and paper, glass, electronic components, software and building products.
markets: Operates worldwide through Georgia-Pacific, Molex, Guardian Industries, INVISTA, Flint Hills Resources and Infor, with sites in many countries.
rationale: B2B-heavy group; technology units such as Molex and Infor could use F1 for showcase and hospitality, but the group rarely sponsors sport.

name: Robert Bosch GmbH
desc: Makes automotive components, power tools, household appliances, building technology and industrial drives and controls for customers worldwide.
markets: Manufactures and sells across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific; customers include carmakers, tradespeople, households and industry.
rationale: Major automotive supplier with strong tool and appliance consumer brands; F1 offers a technology showcase and B2B hospitality with carmakers.
changed: Completed purchase of the Johnson Controls-Hitachi residential air-conditioning business in 2025.

name: ALDI SÜD Group
desc: Runs Aldi discount supermarkets selling mostly own-label groceries in southern and western Germany and in other countries.
markets: Stores in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Italy, Slovenia, Hungary, the UK, Ireland, the US, Australia and China.
rationale: Mass-market brand in key F1 markets (UK, US, Australia, Italy); reach is relevant, though discounters spend little on premium sport.

name: INA-Holding Schaeffler GmbH & Co. KG
desc: Family holding company controlling Schaeffler AG, maker of bearings, engine, transmission, chassis and electric drive components.
markets: Through Schaeffler AG (listed in Frankfurt), plants and customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific in automotive and industrial markets.
rationale: Schaeffler has long motorsport involvement in DTM and Formula E; F1 could showcase drivetrain technology to carmakers and industrial buyers.
changed: Schaeffler AG merged with Vitesco Technologies in 2024.

name: PHOENIX Pharma SE
desc: Wholesales medicines to pharmacies and runs retail pharmacy chains, under brands such as BENU, across Europe.
markets: Wholesale and pharmacy operations in many European countries; no verified operations outside Europe.
rationale: Regulated pharmaceutical distributor serving pharmacies; limited marketing culture makes F1 a weak fit.

name: Louis Dreyfus Company B.V.
desc: Trades and processes grains, oilseeds, coffee, cotton, sugar, rice and other agricultural commodities for food and feed customers.
markets: Merchandising and processing operations across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B commodity merchant with little consumer branding; F1 fit is weak beyond possible Gulf-market client hospitality.
changed: Abu Dhabi's ADQ bought a 45% stake in 2021; Louis Dreyfus family holding keeps control.

name: Mars, Incorporated
desc: Makes confectionery, snacks and pet food brands such as M&M's, Snickers and Royal Canin, and runs veterinary clinics.
markets: Sells worldwide across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and Africa; veterinary hospitals mainly in the US and Europe.
rationale: Global consumer brands with heavy sports marketing; rivals Nestlé (KitKat) and PepsiCo already sponsor F1, so a partnership fits.
changed: Completed acquisition of Kellanova (Pringles, Cheez-It) in 2025.

name: H-E-B (H.E. Butt Grocery Company)
desc: Operates supermarkets and grocery stores in Texas and northern Mexico, selling groceries, pharmacy items and own-label products.
markets: Stores in Texas and northern Mexico only; no verified expansion beyond these markets.
rationale: Strong Texas brand; the United States Grand Prix in Austin is in its core market, suiting local activation rather than global deals.

name: Reyes Holdings, L.L.C.
desc: Distributes beer and Coca-Cola beverages in the US and supplies food and packaging to McDonald's restaurants through Martin Brower.
markets: Beer and Coca-Cola distribution in several US states; Martin Brower serves McDonald's restaurants in several countries outside the US.
rationale: B2B distributor with little need for its own brand marketing; beverage partners could use F1 hospitality, but the fit is weak.

name: Enterprise Mobility
desc: Rents cars and trucks and provides car sharing and fleet management under the Enterprise, National and Alamo brands.
markets: Operates in more than 90 countries and territories, mainly North America and Europe, with franchise operators elsewhere.
rationale: Global travel and mobility brand serving race-weekend travellers; F1 could build brand awareness in the US, Europe and new markets.
changed: Renamed Enterprise Mobility (from Enterprise Holdings) in 2023.

name: Sonepar
desc: Distributes electrical products, automation equipment and related supplies to electrical installers, contractors and industrial customers.
markets: Distribution businesses across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: B2B distributor whose suppliers Schneider Electric and Siemens sponsor F1; hospitality for installers and supplier co-marketing is plausible.

name: Groupe Auchan (ELO)
desc: Runs Auchan hypermarkets, supermarkets and convenience stores in France, other European countries and parts of Africa.
markets: Stores in France and several other European countries plus franchised stores in Africa; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Mass-market French grocer; F1 offers limited value beyond French consumers and supplier hospitality, so the fit is weak.
changed: Family holding company renamed ELO in 2020.

name: Mercadona, S.A.
desc: Runs supermarkets in Spain and Portugal selling groceries and household goods, largely under its Hacendado own label.
markets: Stores in Spain and Portugal only; no verified plans beyond the Iberian Peninsula.
rationale: Domestic-focused grocer with limited sponsorship culture; only Spanish F1 fans are relevant, so the fit is weak.

name: C&S Wholesale Grocers, LLC
desc: Supplies groceries and related products wholesale to supermarket chains and independent grocers across the United States.
markets: Customers and warehouses in the United States only; no verified international activity.
rationale: B2B grocery wholesaler with no consumer brand to promote; F1 is a weak fit.
changed: Planned purchase of stores from the Kroger-Albertsons merger lapsed when that merger was blocked in 2024.

name: Groupe Lactalis
desc: Makes milk, cheese, butter, yoghurt and other dairy products under brands such as Président, Galbani and Parmalat.
markets: Plants and sales across Europe, the Americas, Africa, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global dairy brands sold in F1 markets such as Italy, the US and Australia; plausible for brand campaigns, though dairy rarely sponsors F1.
changed: Acquired General Mills' US yogurt business in 2025.

name: Heraeus Group
desc: Technology group working in precious metals trading and recycling, medical components, electronics materials, quartz glass and sensors.
markets: Operations and customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B materials and electronics supplier; F1 could serve a technology showcase and client hospitality, but consumer brand value is low.

name: C.H. Boehringer Sohn AG & Co. KG (Boehringer Ingelheim)
desc: Parent of Boehringer Ingelheim, which develops and makes prescription medicines for humans and animal health products.
markets: Sells human and animal health products across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Prescription drug maker facing strict advertising rules; F1 brand value is limited beyond animal health or employer branding.

name: Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores
desc: Runs highway travel stops and convenience stores selling fuel, food and truck services across the United States.
markets: Locations in US states only; no verified international activity.
rationale: US-only fuel and travel retailer; F1 offers little beyond US race activations, so the fit is weak.

name: Southern Glazer's Wine & Spirits
desc: Distributes wine, spirits and beer from producers to retailers, bars, restaurants and hotels in the United States and Canada.
markets: Distribution in most US states and in Canada; no verified expansion beyond North America.
rationale: Distributes spirits for brands active in F1; based in Miami, so the Miami and Las Vegas races offer trade hospitality.

name: RETHMANN SE & Co. KG
desc: Family group running Remondis recycling and water services, Rhenus logistics, Saria animal by-product processing and Transdev public transport.
markets: Operations in Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and other regions through Remondis, Rhenus, Saria and Transdev.
rationale: Rhenus logistics could use F1 to show freight capability and host B2B clients, though the group rarely does sports marketing.

name: Cox Enterprises, Inc.
desc: Owns Cox Communications cable and broadband and Cox Automotive, including Manheim auctions, Autotrader and Kelley Blue Book.
markets: Broadband in US states; Cox Automotive mainly in the US with some operations in Europe and Australia.
rationale: US broadband and car-marketplace brands; F1's growing US audience suits Autotrader and Kelley Blue Book marketing.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to combine Cox Communications with Charter Communications; completion not confirmed.

name: Adolf Würth GmbH & Co. KG
desc: Sells fasteners, screws, tools, chemicals and assembly materials to tradespeople, workshops and industrial customers worldwide.
markets: Companies in more than 80 countries across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Automotive workshop and trade customers suit motorsport; F1 visibility and hospitality could support its large sales force in many markets.

name: Meijer, Inc.
desc: Runs supercenters and grocery stores selling food, general merchandise and pharmacy services in the US Midwest.
markets: Stores in Midwestern US states only; no verified international activity.
rationale: Regional US retailer with no presence near F1 events; the fit is weak.

name: Gordon Food Service, Inc.
desc: Distributes food and supplies to restaurants, schools, hospitals and other institutions, and runs Gordon Food Service retail stores.
markets: Customers in the United States and Canada; no verified expansion beyond North America.
rationale: B2B food distributor with limited consumer marketing; F1 is a weak fit.

name: QuikTrip Corporation
desc: Runs convenience stores and fuel stations selling gasoline, diesel, snacks, drinks and made-to-order food in US states.
markets: Stores in several US states only; no verified international activity.
rationale: US-only convenience retailer; F1 offers little beyond local race-market activation, so the fit is weak.

name: JM Family Enterprises, Inc.
desc: Distributes Toyota vehicles to dealers in five southeastern states and runs car dealerships, auto finance and warranty businesses.
markets: Customers in the southeastern United States through Southeast Toyota Distributors; no verified international activity.
rationale: Florida-based Toyota distributor; the Miami Grand Prix and Toyota's Haas tie-up give a local activation angle.
f1: Independent distributor of Toyota vehicles (Toyota Gazoo Racing is title partner of the Haas F1 team); no F1 deal of its own known.

name: RaceTrac, Inc.
desc: Runs convenience stores and fuel stations under the RaceTrac and RaceWay brands in the southern United States.
markets: Stores in southern US states only; no verified international activity.
rationale: US-only convenience retailer; despite the name, F1 offers little beyond local race-market activation.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to acquire the Potbelly sandwich chain.

name: Wawa, Inc.
desc: Runs convenience stores and fuel stations selling made-to-order food, coffee and gasoline in the eastern United States.
markets: Stores in eastern US states only; expanding into new US states, with no verified international activity.
rationale: US-only convenience retailer with no presence near F1 races except Florida; the fit is weak.

name: DKV Mobility Group
desc: Provides fuel cards, toll boxes, EV charging access and payment services for truck and car fleets across Europe.
industry: fleet fuel cards and toll payments
markets: Customers and acceptance network across European countries; no verified operations outside Europe.
rationale: B2B payments brand serving European fleets; F1 hospitality and mobility-themed activation are plausible but not an obvious fit.

name: Tetra Laval Group
desc: Parent of Tetra Pak food packaging, Sidel bottling equipment and DeLaval dairy farming equipment, sold to food producers worldwide.
markets: Sales and plants across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, Africa and the Middle East.
rationale: B2B packaging supplier to drinks and food brands that sponsor F1; hospitality and sustainability messaging plausible, consumer value limited.

name: Yıldız Holding
desc: Food group owning Ülker and pladis biscuits and snacks, including McVitie's, plus Godiva chocolates.
markets: Türkiye, the UK and many export markets in Europe, the Middle East, Asia and the Americas through pladis and Godiva.
rationale: Brands with wide reach (McVitie's, Godiva) and a large Turkish home market; F1 could support premium chocolate or snack campaigns.

name: dm-drogerie markt GmbH + Co. KG
desc: Runs drugstores selling cosmetics, personal care, health, baby and household products, many under own labels, in Europe.
markets: Stores in Germany, Austria and other Central and South-East European countries; no verified plans outside Europe.
rationale: European drugstore chain with modest sports marketing; F1 is a weak fit beyond Austrian and Hungarian race markets.

name: Knauf Gips KG
desc: Makes plasterboard, gypsum plasters, insulation and other dry-construction building materials for builders worldwide.
markets: Plants and sales across Europe, the Americas (including USG), Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: B2B building-materials maker; F1 hospitality for contractors and distributors plausible, but little consumer brand value.

name: United Shipping & Trading Company (USTC)
desc: Group trading marine fuels through Bunker Holding and running shipping, tanker and other businesses.
markets: Bunker trading offices and shipping customers across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: B2B marine fuel trader with no consumer brand; F1 fit is weak beyond client hospitality.

name: SPAR Holding AG
desc: Runs SPAR, EUROSPAR and INTERSPAR supermarkets and hypermarkets in Austria, Slovenia, Hungary, Croatia and northern Italy.
markets: Stores in Austria, Slovenia, Hungary, Croatia and northern Italy; no verified plans beyond Central Europe.
rationale: Central European grocer; Austrian and Hungarian Grands Prix give some local relevance, but overall F1 fit is weak.

name: Emil Frey Holding AG
desc: Imports and sells cars through dealerships across Europe and provides servicing, parts and vehicle financing.
markets: Dealerships and import businesses in Switzerland, Germany, France, the UK and other European countries.
rationale: Car retailer for many brands active in F1 and owner of a GT racing team; F1 hospitality for buyers fits well.

name: Otto Group
desc: Runs online retailers such as otto.de and Crate & Barrel, plus logistics (Hermes) and financial services (EOS).
markets: Germany and other European countries, plus North America through Crate & Barrel; some services in other regions.
rationale: Large German e-commerce brand; F1 could support otto.de reach, but the group has little motorsport history.
changed: Sold its About You stake to Zalando in 2025.

name: Jim Pattison Group Inc.
desc: Canadian conglomerate owning Save-On-Foods grocery stores, car dealerships, packaging, media, signs and Ripley's Believe It or Not.
markets: Mainly Canada and the US, with Ripley's and Guinness World Records operating in other countries.
rationale: Mostly Western Canadian retail and dealerships; the Canadian Grand Prix is the only clear angle, so the fit is weak.

name: Yazaki Corporation
desc: Makes automotive wiring harnesses, connectors, instruments and electric wire, plus gas and solar equipment for buildings.
markets: Plants and customers across Asia-Pacific, the Americas and Europe, serving Japanese and Western carmakers.
rationale: Global automotive supplier; F1 could offer B2B hospitality with carmakers such as Honda and Toyota and a technology story.

name: Liebherr Group
desc: Makes cranes, earthmoving and mining machinery, refrigerators, aerospace and transport systems, machine tools and components.
markets: Plants and sales across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, Africa and the Middle East.
rationale: Engineering brand with consumer fridges and B2B machinery; an F1 engineering showcase and hospitality is plausible but not obvious.

name: Marquard & Bahls AG
desc: Trades and supplies oil products and fuels, and provides aviation fuelling services through companies such as Mabanaft and Skytanking.
markets: Fuel trading and supply in Europe and North America; aviation fuelling at airports in several countries.
rationale: B2B fuel trader without a consumer brand; F1 fit is weak beyond hospitality.

name: Dirk Rossmann GmbH
desc: Runs drugstores selling cosmetics, personal care, health and household products in Germany and several other countries.
markets: Stores in Germany, Poland, Czechia, Hungary, Türkiye and other European countries; no verified plans outside the region.
rationale: European drugstore chain with a domestic marketing focus; F1 is a weak fit beyond the Hungarian race market.

name: Reitan AS
desc: Retail group running REMA 1000 supermarkets and Narvesen, 7-Eleven and other convenience stores in Nordic and Baltic countries.
markets: Stores in Norway, Denmark, Sweden, Finland and the Baltic states; no verified plans outside Northern Europe.
rationale: Nordic grocer and convenience retailer; F1 has limited relevance in its markets, so the fit is weak.

name: Sheetz, Inc.
desc: Runs convenience stores and fuel stations with made-to-order food in Pennsylvania and other mid-Atlantic and Midwestern states.
markets: Stores in several US states only; no verified international activity.
rationale: US-only convenience retailer with no F1 race in its region; the fit is weak.

name: Wanxiang Group
desc: Makes automotive parts such as universal joints, bearings and brakes, plus lithium batteries and electric vehicle components.
markets: China plus operations in the United States through Wanxiang America and A123 Systems, and sales in other markets.
rationale: Chinese parts and battery maker with US operations; the Chinese Grand Prix and a technology story make F1 plausible but not obvious.

name: Menard, Inc. (Menards)
desc: Runs Menards home improvement stores selling building materials, hardware, groceries and household goods in Midwestern US states.
markets: Stores in Midwestern US states only; no verified international activity.
rationale: Regional US retailer whose motorsport spending has gone to US series such as NASCAR; F1 is a weak fit.

name: Freudenberg & Co. KG
desc: Makes seals, vibration control parts, filters, nonwovens and medical products, plus Vileda household cleaning products.
markets: Plants and customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific in automotive, industrial and consumer markets.
rationale: Technology supplier to carmakers and industry; F1 engineering showcase and hospitality plausible, consumer value mainly through Vileda.

name: Wegmans Food Markets, Inc.
desc: Runs supermarkets selling groceries, prepared foods and pharmacy products in the northeastern and mid-Atlantic United States.
markets: Stores in north-eastern and mid-Atlantic US states only; no verified international activity.
rationale: Regional US grocer with no F1 race in its region; the fit is weak.

name: Axel Johnson AB
desc: Family group holding a controlling stake in grocer Axfood plus industrial trading, services and consumer retail businesses.
markets: Mainly Sweden and other Nordic countries, with industrial trading businesses elsewhere in Europe.
rationale: Nordic-focused group whose grocery and industrial brands sell mainly at home; F1 offers little commercial value, so the fit is weak.

name: Ashley Furniture Industries, LLC
desc: Designs, makes and sells home furniture, mattresses and decor through Ashley stores, online and other retailers.
markets: Mainly the United States, with licensed Ashley stores and dealers in many other countries.
rationale: Consumer brand with heavy US advertising and licensed stores abroad; F1's growing US audience could support brand reach.

name: Koninklijke Jumbo Food Groep (Jumbo)
desc: Runs Jumbo supermarkets and online grocery delivery in the Netherlands and Belgium.
markets: Stores in the Netherlands and Belgium only; no verified plans beyond the Benelux.
rationale: Has sponsored Max Verstappen personally and Dutch motorsport events; Dutch F1 popularity makes a partnership plausible.

name: The Hearst Corporation
desc: Publishes magazines and newspapers, owns TV stations and stakes in cable networks, and provides business information through Fitch.
markets: US media plus magazine editions and Fitch ratings operations across Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: Owns motoring titles Car and Driver and Road & Track; F1 media partnerships and advertising tie-ins are plausible.

name: Danfoss A/S
desc: Makes heating and cooling components, power electronics, drives and mobile hydraulics for buildings, industry and off-highway machines.
markets: Plants and customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B engineering group with an energy-efficiency story; F1 sustainability and hospitality angle plausible but not obvious.

name: Giant Eagle, Inc.
desc: Runs supermarkets and pharmacies in Pennsylvania, Ohio and neighbouring states under the Giant Eagle and Market District brands.
markets: Stores in Pennsylvania, Ohio, West Virginia, Maryland and Indiana; no verified international activity.
rationale: Regional US grocer with no F1 race in its region; the fit is weak.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to sell its GetGo convenience stores to Alimentation Couche-Tard.

name: Takenaka Corporation
desc: General contractor designing and building offices, stadiums, hospitals and other large buildings in Japan and abroad.
markets: Mainly Japan, with offices and projects in South-East Asia, China, Europe and the United States.
rationale: B2B builder with little brand marketing abroad; the Japanese Grand Prix is a minor angle, so the fit is weak.

name: S.C. Johnson & Son, Inc. (SC Johnson)
desc: Makes household cleaning, pest control, air care and storage products sold under brands such as Glade, Raid, Windex and Ziploc.
markets: Sells in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and Africa.
rationale: Global household brands sold in F1 markets; F1 could give brand visibility, plausible though not an obvious category fit.

name: Gulf States Toyota, Inc.
desc: Distributes new Toyota vehicles, parts and accessories to dealers in Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Louisiana and Mississippi.
markets: Dealers in five south-central US states; no verified international activity.
rationale: Texas-based Toyota distributor; the US Grand Prix in Austin and Toyota's Haas partnership give a local angle.
f1: Independent distributor of Toyota vehicles (Toyota Gazoo Racing is title partner of the Haas F1 team); no F1 deal of its own known.

name: Standard Industries, Inc.
desc: Holding company owning roofing maker GAF, European roofing firm BMI, chemicals maker W. R. Grace and other businesses.
markets: North America and Europe through GAF and BMI, with Grace and other units selling worldwide.
rationale: Roofing brands with consumer advertising in the US and Europe; F1 hospitality and brand reach plausible but not obvious.

name: Pon Holdings B.V.
desc: Imports and sells Volkswagen Group cars in the Netherlands, distributes Caterpillar equipment and makes bicycles such as Gazelle and Cervélo.
markets: Netherlands and other European countries, plus Caterpillar dealerships and bicycle brands selling in North America and elsewhere.
rationale: Dutch importer of Audi and other F1-linked car brands with strong Dutch F1 interest; hospitality and brand co-marketing fit well.
f1: Dutch importer of Volkswagen Group brands including Audi, which runs an F1 team from 2026; no F1 deal of its own known.

name: NorgesGruppen ASA
desc: Runs Norway's largest grocery retail chains, including KIWI, Meny and Spar, and grocery wholesale operations.
markets: Customers in Norway only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic Norwegian grocer; F1 offers little commercial value, so the fit is weak.

name: McCain Foods Limited
desc: Makes frozen french fries, potato specialties and appetisers for restaurants, foodservice operators and supermarkets worldwide.
markets: Plants and sales across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and Africa.
rationale: Global food brand with retail and foodservice reach; F1 is plausible for consumer campaigns but not an obvious category fit.

name: Italiana Petroli S.p.A.
desc: Runs the IP fuel station network in Italy and refines, stores and markets petroleum products.
markets: Customers in Italy only; no verified international activity.
rationale: Italian fuel brand whose rival Eni sponsors F1; Monza and Imola give home-market relevance for consumer and B2B activation.
changed: Reported in 2025 to be in sale talks with Azerbaijan's SOCAR; outcome not confirmed.

name: Globus Holding GmbH & Co. KG
desc: Runs Globus hypermarkets and Globus Baumarkt DIY stores in Germany, Luxembourg, Czechia and other countries.
markets: Stores in Germany and a few other European countries; no verified plans outside Europe.
rationale: Regional German retailer; F1 has little commercial value for it, so the fit is weak.

name: E/D/E (Einkaufsbüro Deutscher Eisenhändler GmbH)
desc: Purchasing and marketing association negotiating supply, logistics and payment services for independent tool, hardware and building-supply dealers.
markets: Member dealers in Germany and other European countries; no verified activity outside Europe.
rationale: Purchasing association owned by member dealers with no consumer brand; F1 fit is weak.

name: Theo Müller Group (Unternehmensgruppe Theo Müller)
desc: Makes yoghurts, milk drinks, desserts and other dairy products under brands such as Müller, Weihenstephan and Müllermilch.
markets: Mainly Germany, the UK and other European countries, with exports beyond Europe.
rationale: Consumer dairy brands in European F1 markets such as the UK and Germany; plausible but not an obvious fit.

name: Kohler Co.
desc: Makes kitchen and bathroom fixtures, faucets and tiles, and runs luxury hotels and golf resorts.
markets: Sells across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions; hospitality mainly in Wisconsin and Scotland.
rationale: Premium kitchen and bath brand with luxury hospitality; F1's affluent audience suits it in the US, Europe and Asia.
changed: Sold a majority of its energy business (now Rehlko) to Platinum Equity in 2024.

name: Visy Industries Holdings
desc: Makes cardboard boxes, paper, glass bottles and aluminium cans, and recycles paper and plastics in Australia.
markets: Mainly Australia and New Zealand; exports recycled materials and products to Asia.
rationale: B2B packaging and recycling firm; the Australian Grand Prix in Melbourne offers hospitality, but the fit is weak.

name: Sucden (Sucres et Denrées)
desc: Trades sugar, cocoa, coffee, ethanol and other soft commodities, and provides commodity brokerage services.
markets: Trading offices across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and Africa.
rationale: B2B soft-commodity trader with no consumer brand to promote; F1 fit is weak beyond occasional client hospitality.

name: J.R. Simplot Company
desc: Makes frozen potato products and fertiliser, grows crops and raises cattle, and supplies food to restaurant chains.
markets: Mainly the United States, with operations in Canada, Australia, China and other markets.
rationale: Mostly B2B food and farm supplier to restaurant chains and growers, with little consumer branding; F1 fit is weak.

name: Benteler International AG
desc: Makes chassis, body and engine components for carmakers and steel tubes for automotive, energy and industrial uses.
markets: Plants and customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Automotive supplier selling to carmakers; F1 B2B hospitality and lightweight-engineering showcase plausible but not obvious.

name: B. Braun SE
desc: Makes infusion systems, surgical instruments, wound care and other hospital products, and runs dialysis clinics.
markets: Sells across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and Africa.
rationale: Hospital supplier selling to clinicians, with little consumer marketing; F1 fit is weak.

name: Wilhelm Hoyer B.V. & Co. KG
desc: Sells heating oil, diesel, lubricants and energy services to households and businesses, and runs fuel stations in Germany.
markets: Customers mainly in Germany; no verified international activity.
rationale: Regional German fuel distributor; F1 offers little commercial value, so the fit is weak.

name: Perdue Farms Inc.
desc: Produces chicken and turkey products, and supplies grain and agricultural services through its agribusiness unit.
markets: Customers mainly in the United States, with some exports; no verified international operations.
rationale: US food brand with domestic focus; F1 offers limited value, so the fit is weak.

name: Landmark Group
desc: Runs fashion, footwear, home, electronics and budget retail chains such as Centrepoint, Max and Home Centre.
markets: Stores across the Gulf states, wider Middle East and India, plus other markets.
rationale: Large consumer retailer in Gulf and Indian markets; Abu Dhabi, Saudi and Qatar Grands Prix offer home-market activation.

name: Deichmann SE
desc: Runs shoe store chains, including Deichmann in Europe and Rack Room Shoes in the US, selling affordable footwear.
markets: Stores in many European countries and in the US through Rack Room Shoes.
rationale: Mass-market shoe retailer with sports-footwear sales; F1 is plausible for brand reach in Europe but not obvious.

name: Esselunga S.p.A.
desc: Runs supermarkets and superstores in northern and central Italy and offers online grocery delivery.
markets: Stores in Italy only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Italian grocer near Monza; F1 offers some home-market visibility, but the fit is weak for a domestic grocer.

name: Central National-Gottesman Inc.
desc: Distributes pulp, paper, paperboard, packaging and tissue products to manufacturers, printers and converters worldwide.
markets: Sales offices and customers across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: B2B paper and pulp distributor with no consumer brand to promote; F1 fit is weak beyond client hospitality.

name: Tengelmann Group
desc: Family group owning OBI home improvement stores, the KiK textile discounter and other retail and venture investments.
markets: OBI and KiK stores in Germany and other European countries; no verified operations outside Europe.
rationale: European retail brands with mass-market reach; F1 is a weak fit beyond regional brand visibility.

name: Murugappa Group
desc: Indian group whose companies make bicycles, abrasives, fertilisers and sugar, and provide vehicle finance and insurance.
markets: Mainly India, with abrasives and other subsidiaries in Russia, South Africa and other countries.
rationale: India-focused group with listed consumer and finance brands; no Indian Grand Prix, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Dyson Technology Ltd.
desc: Designs and sells vacuum cleaners, hair care tools, fans, air purifiers and lighting under the Dyson brand.
markets: Sells across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East; group head office in Singapore.
rationale: Engineering-led premium brand selling in F1's key markets; direct rival SharkNinja sponsors F1, so a technology partnership fits.
changed: Group head office moved to Singapore in 2019.

name: AMAGGI (Grupo André Maggi)
desc: Grows soybeans, corn and cotton, trades and exports grain, and runs river logistics and energy businesses in Brazil.
markets: Farms and logistics in Brazil; exports grain mainly to Asia and Europe.
rationale: B2B agribusiness with no consumer brand; the Brazilian Grand Prix gives a minor angle, so fit is weak.

name: Discount Tire (America's Tire)
desc: Sells tires and wheels and provides installation and related services through stores across the United States and online.
markets: Stores in US states only; no verified international activity.
rationale: US tire retailer with motorsport-adjacent customers; F1's US races give some relevance, but the fit is weak.

name: Hancock Prospecting Pty Ltd
desc: Mines and exports iron ore through Roy Hill and other joint ventures, and owns cattle stations and other agricultural assets.
markets: Mines and farms in Australia; iron ore sold mainly to steelmakers in Asia.
rationale: B2B miner with no consumer brand; F1 fit is weak beyond client hospitality.

name: 84 Lumber Company
